title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
abstract: arXiv:2610.13437v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score

translated_title: 面向高亮度大型强子对撞机（HL-LHC）异常检测的学习型事件表征的局部诊断方法
translated_abstract: 异常检测，即识别偏离标准模型预期的碰撞事件，是在大型强子对撞机（LHC）上进行新物理搜索中最具前景的模型无关策略之一。在学习得到的低维表征中搜索稀有事件，可以免去事先依赖手工设计的可观测量，但也牺牲了这些可观测量所提供的直接物理解释。因此，要使异常检测能够进入发现流程，必须对被标记的事件进行局部诊断：一方面要区分潜在的新物理与错误建模或探测器效应，另一方面要识别出可用于后续定向搜索的可观测量。我们在COLLIDE-2V数据集上评估了监督式和自监督式神经嵌入策略，该数据集是在高亮度LHC真实条件下模拟的、包含7.5亿事件的大规模数据集，并使用在学习的潜空间中训练的自编码器的重构误差作为异常评分。
tldr: 该论文在高亮度LHC条件下模拟的7.5亿事件数据集COLLIDE-2V上，评估了监督与自监督神经嵌入策略，并以学习潜空间中自编码器的重构误差作为异常评分，强调必须对被标记事件进行局部诊断，以区分新物理与建模误差或探测器效应，并为后续定向搜索识别可观测量。
en_tdlr: This paper evaluates supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic HL-LHC conditions, using autoencoder reconstruction error in the learned latent space as the anomaly score, and emphasizes that flagged events must be locally diagnosed to distinguish new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches.
